items.title: Trapped nine days in a dark tunnel, Nepali man tells his survival story
items.blurb: Rescued after 10 days underground, Sanjay Sah says prayer, hope and thoughts of his family helped him endure the darkness, hunger and injuries.

items.title: Flood damage leaves Rasuwagadhi road facing long repairs
items.blurb: The Department of Roads is opening temporary tracks and planning Bailey bridges after the Bhotekoshi flood washed away about 40 km of road, while officials aim to restore a link to the Chinese border before Dashain.

items.title: Farmers face dire consequences as floods devastate Nepal’s harvest
items.blurb: Farmers affected by this disaster are the same people who help put food on our tables every day.

items.title: Bhotekoshi floods push Kulekhani into continuous power generation
items.blurb: National power generation has lost over 400 megawatts following the August 26 floods.

items.title: August flood death toll rises to 1386, with 5130 still missing
items.blurb: Authorities have recovered 1,386 bodies from eight districts affected by the August 26 Bhotekoshi floods, but only 104 have been identified and handed over to families.

items.title: Korala border customs revenue surges as cargo diverts from closed crossings
items.blurb: Customs collected Rs1.5 billion in 15 days after the August floods closed the Rasuwagadhi and Tatopani crossings, while transport costs to Kathmandu have risen 15-fold.

items.title: What a telecom licence means—and what happens when it expires
items.blurb: UTL’s licence has been cancelled for non-payment. What does a telecom licence allow—and what happens when an operator fails to meet its obligations?

items.title: Indian TV coverage of Nepal floods criticised for sensationalism
items.blurb: Residents say some crews have turned their own difficulties at disaster sites into television drama and given less attention to those flood victims.

items.title: Book Review: An ice factory, the great famine and the mystery of missing Dalit workers
items.blurb: In ‘White Elephant’, we are made to confront the oppressors of our own time and, unnervingly, the oppressor within ourselves.

items.title: What’s on in Kathmandu Valley this week
items.blurb: Art, music, workshops, and community events to check out across the Valley, including fundraisers for flood-affected communities.

items.title: UTL licence lapses, company seeks more time to clear Rs31 billion dues
items.blurb: The telecommunications company missed its September 4 renewal deadline after failing to pay its renewal fee and outstanding dues. The government says it must pay all dues to renew its licence.

items.title: Saptari childbirth on street outside hospital raises questions over Nepal’s free maternity care
items.blurb: A woman giving birth on a pavement outside a government hospital after her husband could not afford Rs3,200 in tests exposes the gap between Nepal’s free maternity care and access to emergency healthcare.

items.title: Decade-old alternative to a vital Prithvi Highway link remains on paper
items.blurb: The collapse-prone Krishnabhir section of the Prithvi Highway has exposed the lack of a parallel route on the other side of the Trishuli river, despite plans dating back nearly a decade.

items.title: Philippine ferry fire death toll jumps to 35
items.blurb: Thick smoke and extreme heat had earlier prevented rescuers from entering the ferry, which was carrying more than 130 people when it was engulfed in flames.

items.title: Prime Minister Shah to highlight Nepal’s outsized climate burden at UN
items.blurb: Following devastating Bhotekoshi floods, Shah will press for financial support to help Nepal recover and build climate resilience.

items.title: Water starts flowing through landslide-dammed Hunga Khola, easing flood risk
items.blurb: Authorities had warned of possible flooding downstream after a landslide blocked the river in Solukhumbu and formed a roughly 100-metre-long dam on Friday morning.

items.title: Nepal estimates Rs2.34 billion to rebuild flood-hit education sector
items.blurb: Eighteen schools were affected in Rasuwa, disrupting classes for more than 9,000 students after the August 26 Bhotekoshi floods.
